html:
The Laotian Civil War was fought from 1959 to 1975 between the Royal Lao Government and the communist Pathet Lao, backed by North Vietnam. It was part of the wider Vietnam War.

Neutralist governments and peace deals in 1962 and 1973 failed. North Vietnam used eastern Laos for the Ho Chi Minh trail, and the United States answered with a secret war: bombing and a CIA-backed army of Hmong fighters.

After the fall of Saigon in 1975, the Pathet Lao took power peacefully, abolished the monarchy and founded the Lao People's Democratic Republic on 2 December 1975 under Kaysone Phomvihane. Many Hmong fled; see Hmong exodus.
